name: Iroas
description: God of warfare and patron of the Akroans, who grapples with his twin Mogis in the sky above Akros.

timeline.summary: Iroas and Mogis appear as stars above Akros and grapple, absorbed in their own conflict and not helping mortals.
timeline.quote: The twins were interested in each other, not mortals.

timeline.summary: The nyxborn blesses Aesrias with Iroas's power, healing him and strengthening him before he faces sirens; Aesrias asks for candle wax for his ears.
timeline.quote: He touched my shoulders. And I felt better. My wounds healed. I was no longer tired.

timeline.summary: Zosimos, walking by the woods, is overtaken by worry that he will never gain the glory and favor of the gods like other heroes.
timeline.quote: What if he died having never gained the favor of the gods?

timeline.summary: A satyr springs onto the path, tells Zosimos his mind's garden is full of weeds, and says worry is Phenax's creation that spurns Iroas.
timeline.quote: When you worry, you're actually worshipping Phenax.

relations.note: Mogis is the dark twin of Iroas, and both govern the domain of war.
relations.quote: Mogis, the dark twin of the god Iroas, is the horned god of wrath and pain.

relations.note: Iroas is patron god of the Akroans.
relations.quote: respective patrons of the Akroans and the minotaurs

relations.note: Twin gods locked in a long conflict.
relations.quote: They grappled in the sky, fighting the latest battle in their long and brutal conflict.
I am one of many who are blessed with the might of Iroas

relations.note: The nyxborn says both it and Aesrias serve Iroas.
relations.quote: You and I both serve Iroas.

pages_say.description: The god Mogis's brother, who thrives on noble tests of mettle and the glory of victory.
God of warfare and patron of the Akroans, who grapples with his twin Mogis in the sky above Akros.
God of Victory who blesses devout families' children with strength to protect people; Aesrias's patron.
A god of whom Aesrias is called the hero.
A god heroes seek to please; the satyr says worshipping Phenax spurns him.
